perspective:
**Keith Ndiaye’s available information:**

- Keith works with Elizabeth at a construction company; he is a construction worker and she is the receptionist. They have a friendly but professional relationship through his office visits for paperwork and project updates.
- Recently, Keith observed Elizabeth being unusually curt with him over several days. He wondered whether he had upset her through a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake.
- Keith asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. She told him no, not at all, and said she was dealing with personal stuff; she apologized if she seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic and offered to listen or talk, suggesting a coffee break. Elizabeth accepted and thanked him.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses. Keith perceived them as quite severe.
- Keith suggested Elizabeth consider talking to a professional, saying an external perspective can sometimes help. Elizabeth said she had thought about it but was not sure and felt hesitant about seeking help.
- After that, Keith noticed Elizabeth became slightly withdrawn. He thought his suggestion might have embarrassed her and felt regretful. He told her he hoped he hadn’t overstepped and that he was there to support her no matter what. Elizabeth replied that he hadn’t overstepped, she appreciated his concern, and it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative. He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him. He said he was glad they talked and that he was always there if she needed to chat or take a break. Elizabeth thanked him, said it meant a lot, and said she felt better knowing she had his support.
